nodes.description: One genotype is published: homozygous missense p.Asp293Asn (NM_006230) in the POLD2 phosphodiesterase domain, absent from ExAC and 1000 Genomes. Structural modelling on the POLD2-POLD3 crystal structure predicts loss of a polar contact with Arg240. No null allele has been seen, and none is expected: POLD2 is essential in yeast and in mammalian cell screens, so a viable patient's allele must be hypomorphic.

nodes.description: The patient has low CD4+ T, B and NK cell counts, and his infections improved on immunoglobulin replacement, so both arms of adaptive immunity are affected. B-cell numbers are low but maturation looks largely intact, with class-switched B cells present and normal somatic hypermutation in IgA and IgG. The humoral deficit is therefore one of numbers, with likely loss of T-cell help, rather than a block in B-cell differentiation. The infection spectrum fits a combined defect: recurrent sinopulmonary bacterial infection with bronchiectasis, recurrent skin abscesses, and chronic molluscum contagiosum, a viral skin infection that needs T cells to clear it. PROVISIONAL because the step from lymphopenia to each infection is inferred from one patient, not measured.

nodes.description: POLD2 is the structural hub of polymerase delta, contacting both POLD1 and POLD3. The p.Asp293Asn protein is turned over faster than wild type, and the patient's stimulated lymphocytes and fibroblasts carry markedly reduced POLD1, POLD2 and POLD3 protein despite normal mRNA. The loss is in the amount of enzyme, not its quality: a complex assembled with the mutant subunit kept normal polymerase activity in a primer-extension assay. The cell therefore has less polymerase delta activity in total, which is what the decreased DNA-directed DNA polymerase activity below records. Re-expressing wild-type POLD2 in the patient's fibroblasts restored POLD1 and POLD3 levels, which places the instability on the POLD2 variant.

nodes.description: The patient's T cells responded poorly to anti-CD3, anti-CD28, PHA and PMA-ionomycin, and after 48 hours of TCR stimulation most remained in G1. Activation markers (CD25, CD95) were upregulated normally and ERK phosphorylation was intact, so TCR signalling works and the defect lies in the replication the cells need to divide. The result held in in-vitro-expanded T cells, which excludes the patient's expanded TEMRA CD8+ population as the explanation. Expanded T cells also carried more 53BP1 foci than controls.

nodes.description: In the patient's fibroblasts, synchronised cells moved through S phase more slowly than control cells. DNA fibre analysis showed fewer new origin firing events and a faster fork speed. Faster forks are read as compensation for the reduced origin firing, the pattern also seen in GINS1 and polymerase epsilon deficiency. The authors attribute it to a rate-limiting amount of an essential replisome component.

nodes.description: Under unchallenged conditions the patient's fibroblasts show ATR checkpoint activation (CHK1 Ser345 and RPA Ser33 phosphorylation), about three times as many gamma-H2AX foci as controls, more RAD51 foci, and more 53BP1 nuclear bodies in G1. The G1 bodies mark under-replicated DNA carried into the next cell cycle. Re-expressing wild-type POLD2 cleared the G1 53BP1 bodies, which establishes that the POLD2 variant causes them. This is replication-derived damage. When the fibroblasts were challenged with a panel of genotoxic agents they were not hypersensitive, so the repair functions of polymerase delta are preserved at the reduced dose.

nodes.description: The patient has short stature and severe intellectual disability with speech impairment, attention deficit and hyperactivity. The authors propose that the same replication-stress mechanism behind the immunodeficiency also explains the neurodevelopmental abnormalities, since polymerase delta is needed by every dividing progenitor. No non-haematopoietic tissue was examined, and with one patient from a consanguineous family a second recessive cause cannot be excluded. The link is therefore recorded as HYPOTHETICAL. The POLD1 patient of the same series has short stature, microcephaly and low IQ, so the developmental features recur across the polymerase delta deficiencies.
